nodes.title: SG-10 Connect Phaser pointer and keyboard events to the game store
nodes.body:
Context: BootScene already emits objectClick (App opens ActionMenu) and re-syncs SceneObjects on every gameStore change. SceneObject already shows hover highlight/label and keyboard focus. Gaps: the typed objectHover event is declared in PhaserToReactEvents but never emitted, and the typed highlightObject event in ReactToPhaserEvents is never consumed. Desired behavior: hover and click flow Phaser to React, store changes (secret door open, inventory) flow back into the scene, and unit tests cover both directions. Why: the Phaser scene and React UI must stay consistent without duplicated state.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a scene object, when the pointer hovers it, then the highlight and label show and objectHover is emitted with its id; on pointer out objectHover carries null
- Given a clicked object, when objectClick is emitted, then App selects it and shows its ActionMenu
- Given a store change such as secret_door_open flag or an inventory item, when the state updates, then every SceneObject receives sync with the new state
- Given a highlightObject event from React, when it is emitted, then the matching scene object takes focus highlight and label and null clears it
- Given unit tests, when run, then they cover Phaser to React and store to Phaser directions


## Scope
- In scope: SceneObject hover listener
- In scope: BootScene objectHover emission and highlightObject subscription
- In scope: Unit tests in both directions
- Out of scope: New assets or content
- Out of scope: Backend or API changes
- Out of scope: Reworking the ActionMenu
- Preserve: Existing objectClick bridge and App ActionMenu
- Preserve: useGameStore as single source of GameState
- Preserve: Phaser mocked in unit tests


## Technical constraints
- Use the typed phaserToReact and reactToPhaser buses in game/frontend/src/phaser/events.ts
- BootScene must not keep its own copy of GameState


## Definition of done
- All three requirements have passing unit tests
- Existing bootScene and appObjectClick tests still pass


## Non-functional requirements
- Subscriptions are released on scene SHUTDOWN


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Hovering a scene object emits a typed objectHover event to React
nodes.body:
Context: SceneObject wires handle.onHover only to highlight and label; PhaserToReactEvents.objectHover exists but nothing emits it. Desired behavior: BootScene forwards hover to the phaserToReact bus. Expected result: React listeners learn which object is hovered. Why: the UI can mirror hover state.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a visible SceneObject, when its handle hover callback fires with true, then onHover listener receives objectId and over true and the highlight and label are shown
- Given a hovered object, when hover fires with false, then BootScene emits objectHover with id null
- Given a hidden object, when hover fires, then no listener call and no highlight occurs


## Scope
- In scope: SceneObject.onHover
- In scope: BootScene hover wiring
- Out of scope: React consumers of objectHover
- Preserve: Existing hover highlight and label behavior
- Preserve: objectClick emission


## Technical constraints
- Event payload shape is { id: string | null }


## Definition of done
- objectHover emitted on hover in and out


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · React highlightObject events drive scene object focus
nodes.body:
Context: ReactToPhaserEvents.highlightObject is declared but unused; SceneObject already has focus() and blur() that show highlight and label. Desired behavior: BootScene subscribes to reactToPhaser highlightObject in create(). Expected result: React can highlight a scene object. Why: completes the React to Phaser direction.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a scene with objects, when highlightObject is emitted with an object id, then that object is focused and all others blurred
- Given a highlighted object, when highlightObject is emitted with null, then every object is blurred
- Given the scene shuts down, when highlightObject is emitted afterwards, then no object is touched


## Scope
- In scope: SceneObject spec id access
- In scope: BootScene highlightObject subscription and cleanup
- Out of scope: Emitting highlightObject from React components
- Preserve: Existing SHUTDOWN cleanup


## Technical constraints
- Reuse SceneObject.focus and blur


## Definition of done
- highlightObject focuses and clears objects; listener removed on shutdown


## Non-functional requirements
- No listener leak across scene restarts


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Store changes such as the secret door and inventory are pushed into the scene
nodes.body:
Context: BootScene.create subscribes to useGameStore and onStateChange calls sync on every SceneObject; SceneObject visibility derives from flag and hasItem conditions. Desired behavior: confirm this path and keep it intact. Expected result: opening the secret door (flag secret_door_open) or gaining an inventory item updates scene visibility. Why: store is the single source of truth.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a created scene, when the store state gains flag secret_door_open true, then every SceneObject.sync is called with that state
- Given a created scene, when the store inventory changes, then every SceneObject.sync is called with the new inventory
- Given a null store state, when onStateChange runs, then no sync is called


## Scope
- In scope: BootScene.onStateChange and subscription
- Out of scope: New content conditions
- Preserve: Subscription release on SHUTDOWN


## Technical constraints
- BootScene reads state only through useGameStore


## Definition of done
- Store to scene sync confirmed and covered


## Clarifying questions
- None

null blurs all; handler removed on shutdown

steps.action: Import reactToPhaser alongside phaserToReact from ./events and add a private field unsubscribeHighlight of type (() => void) | null initialised to null.
steps.code:
import { phaserToReact, reactToPhaser } from './events';
private unsubscribeHighlight: (() => void) | null = null;
steps.expected: File compiles with the new import and field

steps.action: Subscribe to highlightObject: for each scene object call focus() when spec.id equals the payload id, otherwise blur(); store the returned unsubscribe in unsubscribeHighlight.
steps.code: this.unsubscribeHighlight = reactToPhaser.on('highlightObject', ({ id }) => this.sceneObjects.forEach((o) => (o.spec.id === id ? o.focus() : o.blur())));
steps.expected: Emitting highlightObject focuses the matching object and null blurs all

steps.action: Inside the SHUTDOWN callback call this.unsubscribeHighlight?.() and set it to null next to the existing unsubscribe release.
steps.expected: After shutdown highlightObject no longer reaches scene objects
